subject.title: [Bug] Cron Job 使用错误的飞书账号发送消息 - 缺少 accountId 自动推断

question: For cron announce delivery without explicit `delivery.accountId`, should a configured agent/channel binding outrank a same-channel session `lastAccountId`, should disagreement fail closed, or should current session-first compatibility remain?
rationale: The current source and tests intentionally preserve session-first account behavior, but the issue reports wrong-account scheduled delivery across multi-account trust boundaries; automation should not choose that security/compatibility policy alone.

options.title: Adopt binding-aware precedence
options.body: Use explicit cron account first, then a unique configured agent/channel binding, then safe session/default fallbacks, with tests for wrong-account and ambiguous-binding cases.

options.title: Fail closed on disagreement
options.body: Refuse delivery when session-derived and binding-derived accounts disagree, surfacing a diagnostic instead of silently choosing an account.

options.title: Keep session-first compatibility
options.body: Leave `lastAccountId` precedence intact and document that multi-account cron jobs must set `--account` or stored delivery context explicitly.

recommendation.title: Adopt binding-aware precedence
recommendation.body: Use explicit cron account first, then a unique configured agent/channel binding, then safe session/default fallbacks, with tests for wrong-account and ambiguous-binding cases.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest visible history across cron delivery, session routing, and binding helper surfaces involved in the policy decision.
